subject: KineticHealth intermittent interruption claim — investigation concluded
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@kinetichealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embedding pipeline intermittent 5xx / blank responses (batch jobs)

Hi Karthik / Monica,

We observed a short window this morning (approx 09:05–09:08 PT) where several batch embedding jobs against your embeddings endpoint returned HTTP 500 or empty payloads. This affected three of our runs and caused backlog spikes in our ingest pipeline.

Attached is a screenshot of the client errors and a zipped snippet of our request/response logs. We retried the jobs and they succeeded immediately. Can you confirm whether there were any platform incidents or maintenance that could explain this?

Also: our retries are exponential but we'd like to understand whether this is on our side so we can harden the ingest path. Are there known network maintenance windows in your us-west region?

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Senior Platform Engineer
KineticHealth

- We'll try to reproduce with the same request pattern and look for any transient GPU worker restarts or front-door 5xx spikes.

Marissa, Monica — can one of you pick this up and ping Alex if we need more client-side detail?

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@kinetichealth.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 13:03:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Embedding pipeline intermittent 5xx / blank responses (batch jobs)

Alex / team — quick update from our side after a targeted reproduction run:

- We replayed the request payloads you provided against an identical model variant in us-west. We ran 100 repeat batches across the same time distribution and did not observe HTTP 500s or empty bodies.
- Platform metrics (gateway 5xx, worker restarts, infra autoscaler events) show no correlated anomalies for your account or the us-west fleet in that timeframe.
- We did see a small number of client-side TCP retransmits in a separate trace you sent; that suggests a transient network blip between your hosts and the edge.

Action items:
- Can you share the client-side SDK version and whether requests are routed through any proxy/load balancer on your side? Client logs you attached look like the app observed a connection reset in a few cases.
- We’ve attached a short triage note (triage-report-kinetichealth-20270309.pdf) summarizing our tests and metrics snapshots.

If you can share the SDK version and any intermediate network hops, we can continue narrowing this down. From the platform side, we do not see evidence of a service-side outage.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@kinetichealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 08:17:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Embedding pipeline intermittent 5xx / blank responses (batch jobs)

Thanks, Marissa — good to know your reproduction didn't surface the same errors.

We pulled SDK and network details: the affected fleet was running redwood-sdk v1.4.2 behind an internal HAProxy cluster that applies per-host connection pooling. We've uploaded a more detailed client trace to the ZIP (same attachment). The spans show short TCP-level resets for a handful of requests in the same 09:05 window.

We'll also schedule a short network sweep on our side for that time window. Please keep me posted if you find anything else. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@kinetichealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embedding pipeline intermittent 5xx / blank responses (batch jobs) — closure

Alex — following our continued review (including Marissa's reproduction runs and network metric correlation), summary and closure below: 

Summary:
- Timeline: 2027-03-04 09:05–09:08 PT reported by KineticHealth.
- Platform investigation: no gateway-wide 5xx spike, no worker restarts, no deploys, and no autoscaler events during the window.
- Reproduction: multiple targeted replays did not reproduce 5xx/empty payloads.
- Most likely root cause: transient network resets between KineticHealth hosts and the Redwood edge (client-side HAProxy connection pooling + short TCP resets observed in provided traces).

Final actions we took:
- Generated a short internal triage report and attached it (triage-report-kinetichealth-20270309.pdf).
- Recommended mitigations to KineticHealth: upgrade to redwood-sdk >= v1.6.0 (includes connection retry improvements), set conservative per-host connection pool sizes, and add short client-side jitter/backoff for batched uploads.
- Offered a goodwill credit for the affected window; our support team will issue a one-time credit on your next invoice.

If you want, we can schedule a joint 30-minute postmortem with your infra team to walk traces and verify the network configuration. Otherwise we'll consider this incident closed on the Redwood side.

Thanks for the collaboration and the detailed traces — that made the triage straightforward.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
